external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application serving browser requests and placing jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application runs in our web tier.

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker that picks up jobs and performs the heavy work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue where the web application places jobs for the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_stores.notes: The description does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: A database read and written by the background worker; it also stores the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The description does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store from which the web application reads its settings, including its queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store from which the worker reads its settings, including its database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: browser to web application requests
data_flows.description: The browser talks to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: web application to message queue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application places jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: background worker process to message queue picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: background worker process to database access
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: web application to web application config reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: background worker process to worker config reads settings
data_flows.description: The worker reads its settings from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: outside our network
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing the user's browser outside the system's network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The network zone where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The network zone behind the web tier containing the queue, worker and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker is internally exposed because it is in the backend tier behind the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The source places the worker in the backend tier behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a queue-decoupled background process that picks up jobs.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config holds confidential data because it holds the web application's queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config holds confidential data because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds database credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The outside-our-network zone is a network boundary because the browser is outside our network.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the browser sits outside our network.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier is a network boundary because it is distinguished from the backend tier by network location.
assumptions.basis: The source places the web application in the web tier and the backend components behind it.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier is a network boundary because it is a separate tier behind the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the queue, worker and database are in the backend tier behind the web tier.
